Title: Share and collaborate
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-6.5/models/share-and-collaborate
Content: Effective Data Management requires the co-operative efforts of a community of users, collaborating and enriching metadata and models. It is rare to find an organisation where a single person takes responsibility for the definition and management of metadata or models, so the ability to share responsibilities with others is essential. The ability to share content outside the metadata and modelling community is also essential.

Collaboration and ownership are core Solidatus concepts, giving subject matter experts across the organisation power to take ownership of the definition and maintenance of metadata within their respective areas of expertise.

Simple collaboration methods include sharing ownership of models, inviting other users to be authors, and sharing read-only links to models.

More advanced collaboration is supported by Solidatus Activities.
Title: Quick-start guide
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-6.5/get-started/quick-start-guide
Content: There are a few ways to share a model:

From the list in the Model Browser, click the row of a model to go to the Model Overview. Then click the SHARE button that appears on the list of People along the right-hand side. This makes the model visible in the Model Browser for other members of your organization or Groups you belong to.
From the Model Overview, you can also go to the Settings tab and find Permissions to add other people or groups and assign them access roles.
Share a read-only version of a model with other registered Solidatus users by clicking the Share button in the toolbar and copying the link to share with others. You can even apply a specific View to a read-only sharing link, so the model opens to a specific, preserved state when accessed through the link.

Title: Quick-start guide
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-2026.2/get-started/quick-start-guide
Content: There are several ways to share a model:

From the Model Browser, open the model information side panel for a model. Then click the OPEN OVERVIEW button at the bottom of the panel. Find and click the SHARE button that appears on the list of People along the right-hand side. This makes the model visible in the Model Browser for other individuals or Groups registered to your Solidatus environment.
From the Model Overview, you can also go to the Settings tab and find Permissions to add other people or groups and assign them access roles.
From the Model Viewer, you can share a read-only version of a model with other registered Solidatus users by clicking the Share button in the toolbar and copying the link to share with others. You can even apply a specific View to a read-only share link, so the model opens to a specific, preserved state when accessed through the link.
Title: Collaboration concepts and scenarios
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-2026.2/models/share-and-collaborate/collaboration-concepts-and-features
Content: Model Owners can grant permissions to other users by sharing a model via the Summary and Settings tabs on the Model Overview. See Model Roles and Permissions to find out more about the different roles available.

When a model is shared with a user or Group, the default role is Viewer; to allow a user or Group to edit the model directly, they need to have the Owner or Author role.

Model Owners can also give read-only access to other registered Solidatus users by clicking the Share button in the Model Viewer toolbar. See Read-only Sharing for more information.

Owners and Authors can edit and save the model in-situ, without requiring any kind of merging or approval. Take a look below to find out about other ways of sharing the editing workload.

The Practitioner licence allows organisations to extend collaboration beyond the usual modelling community, enabling crowdsourcing of content from the wider community. See Practitioners for more information.

Changes to the roles available for users are notified to each affected user via their list of Notifications
